messages:
Anya (eng-platform): FYI saw a spike: ~200 requests in 5m for tenant=acme routed to model-x-small instead of model-x-prod. Users reporting quality regressions and token truncation.
Ben (eng-runtime): ouch. Any logs or rule matches?
Anya (eng-platform): Log snippet:
```
edge-proxy: incoming req tenant=acme id=... headers=[User-Agent, X-Tenant-Name, X-Tenant-Sig]
edge-rewrite: removed-headers=[X-Tenant-Priority]
route-matcher: matched lane=default-low-capacity
```
Matcher (simplified):
```
- match: headers.X-Tenant-Priority == "reserved"
  lane: prod-heavy
- match: path.prefix == "/v1/"
  lane: default-low-capacity
```
Ben (eng-runtime): That suggests the header rewrite happens before header-based matching. If X-Tenant-Priority is stripped we fall through to the path rule.
Julia (eng-sre): Yep. Precedence bug. Two immediate options: move the header-preserve rewrite earlier, or make the matcher validate X-Tenant-Sig as a signed fallback for priority.
Kevin (product): Customer impact is real for ACME. Short-term mitigation: exempt known reserved tenant IP ranges from the header-stripping rewrite so they keep priority intact. Longer term we need a robust fix.
Anya (eng-platform): Agreed. Short-term patch: add IP exempt list for reserved tenants. Also proposing a router telemetry field to help debugging: `router.degrade_reason` with values like `header_stripped`, `quota_overflow`, `cb_tripped`, `capacity_spill`.
Ben (eng-runtime): Good idea. Also CB currently trips when pool 5xx_rate > 0.05. We should expose `cb.trip_count_by_tenant` and make thresholds tenant-aware. For reserved tenants, require a sustained 30s window or explicit capacity-shed signal before tripping.
Julia (eng-sre): And to avoid cold-start quality hits when spillover happens, warm backup models on capacity spill. Proposed config: 
```
warmup:
  backup_models: true
  cache_kv: true
```
This preloads KV cache and avoids big output regressions when switching to a smaller model.
product-ops: Can the console rollout UX show this? When changing a routing rule, surface the fallback chain, recent `router.degrade_reason` samples, and a diff of sample responses primary vs backup so PMs can see latency/cost/quality tradeoffs.
Anya (eng-platform): Yes. Console changes: (1) per-route "Fallback chain" visual, (2) recent `router.degrade_reason` timeline, (3) sample response diff between primary and backups. We'll add a small CTA to run a canary that exercises the fallback path.
Ben (eng-runtime): I'll own runtime changes: reorder matcher pipeline, add cb metrics, and emit `router.degrade_reason`. Will open a branch with unit + integration tests.
Julia (eng-sre): I'll own the SRE policies: `cb.trip_count_by_tenant` metrics, tenant-aware thresholds, and an alerting/playbook for reserved-tenant error spikes.
Anya (eng-platform): Short-term task list: exempt reserved IPs from rewrite (hotfix), emit `router.degrade_reason` samples, console stub for fallback visual. Tagging @sre-bot to create a monitoring alert if `router.degrade_reason:header_stripped` > 5 occurrences in 10m. :rotating_light:
sre-bot: alert created -> INC-2402137, channel=#incidents, severity=low
Kevin (product): :thumbsup: Please signal when the canary is scheduled and include sample diffs.
Anya (eng-platform): Will do. Opening the short-term patch and a console PR, linking both here when ready.
Ben (eng-runtime): Quick note: update CB docs to state tenant-aware behavior so infra teams know reserved tenants get different trip logic.
Julia (eng-sre): I'll add remediation steps to the rollback playbook: restore header-preserve order or temporarily pin the tenant to prod-heavy lane via a route override.
product-ops: When console diff is live, add a small quality metric (n-gram overlap + hallucination flag) so PMs see the quality delta, not just latency/cost.
Anya (eng-platform): good call. Adding that to the console work item.
Ben (eng-runtime): I'll link the runtime PRs here. Expect tests + canary next week.
Anya (eng-platform): thanks all. Closing the loop once PRs are linked.
